title: Pairing action on canonical configurations
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, let $s$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$, let $u,o$ be Boolean words, let $q,q'$ be optional elements of the eight-state administrative set, and let $i,i'$ be natural numbers with $i,i'\le |x|$. Let $j,j'\in\mathbb Z$, let $m,d\in\{-1,0,1\}$, and let $b$ be an optional bit. If moving the input head from position $i+1$ by $m$ gives position $i'+1$, and $j+d=j'$, then applying the pairing administrative action specified by $m,d,b,q'$ to the canonical pairing configuration specified by $s,u,q,i,j,o$ gives the canonical pairing configuration specified by $s,u,q',i',j',o$ followed by $b$ when $b$ is present.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Boolean Turing machine
$q,q'$ are optional administrative states from the eight-state set
The clamped input-head move from $i+1$ by $m$ equals $i'+1$
replaced:
Applying a pairing administrative action to a canonical pairing configuration
changes only the control state, the two displayed head positions, and the output
(appending the optionally emitted bit); the saved source bank and the captured
word are preserved.
